items.text: Adults 21 and over may buy at licensed dispensaries and possess up to 6 ounces of cannabis and cannabis products. Public consumption isn't allowed; use on private property unless the owner restricts it, or in licensed consumption areas attached to dispensaries (21+, no alcohol or tobacco).

A 2025 state law (P.L.2025, c.215, amended in 2026) brings intoxicating hemp products (THC products made from hemp) under the Cannabis Regulatory Commission. Since 13 April 2026, a product with more than 0.4 mg of total THC per container is no longer treated as hemp; hemp-derived THC products may be sold only by licensed Class 5 cannabis retailers, never online, and never to anyone under 21. Shops with alcohol distribution licences could sell low-dose hemp drinks (no more than 5 mg THC a serving, 10 mg a container) only until 13 November 2026; from 14 November 2026 those drinks are treated as cannabis and sold only by licensed cannabis retailers.

laws.rule: Using a hand-held phone or electronic device while driving a moving vehicle on a public road is illegal; talking, listening, texting and sending messages all count (N.J.S.A. 39:4-97.3). Hands-free use is allowed, and a hand may be used to start or end a function. Hand-held use is allowed only to report an emergency or when the driver fears for their safety. Police can stop a driver for this offence alone.
laws.penalty_signal: US$200 to US$400 first offence, US$400 to US$600 second, US$600 to US$800 third or later, plus 3 licence points and a possible 90-day loss of licence from the third (about A$284 to A$568 for a first offence at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040).

laws.rule: Drivers may not pump their own fuel at New Jersey petrol stations. The Retail Gasoline Dispensing Safety Act (N.J.S.A. 34:3A-4 and following) says only a trained station attendant may dispense fuel into a vehicle or container, and stations must post a notice that serving yourself is unlawful.

New Jersey's Division of Fire Safety says that since 2017 state law permits the sale and use of certain ground-based fireworks, such as hand-held sparklers, smoke devices and party poppers. Aerial fireworks, including bottle rockets, firecrackers and Roman candles, remain prohibited.
